diagnostics.intro: Runtime info to attach to bug reports. Click "Copy" to copy the full report to your clipboard, then paste it into the GitHub issue.
diagnostics.oneDrive: OneDrive interference suspected. Your app data folder appears to be inside a OneDrive-synced location. OneDrive can corrupt SQLite WAL files mid-write, causing silent save failures. To fix this, exclude OpenDraft's data folder from OneDrive backup, or move your Windows AppData folder out of OneDrive sync.

foreignFormat.title: Editing a .{{extension}} file
foreignFormat.saveAsks: Save will ask before overwriting {{name}}. Save As creates a working copy and keeps the source untouched.
foreignFormat.explanation: That file is in another application's format, and it can only hold what that format defines. Saving to it rewrites the file from OpenDraft's copy of the screenplay, so layout details it does not describe may come back slightly differently — and anything OpenDraft keeps alongside the script has nowhere to go:
foreignFormat.keepAll: To keep all of it, use Save As to store the screenplay in OpenDraft's own library instead. The original file stays where it is, untouched.

docxWarning.title: Import from Word — Best-Effort Formatting
docxWarning.detect: OpenDraft will detect screenplay element types (scene heading, action, character, dialogue, parenthetical, transition, etc.) from the Word document's formatting.
docxWarning.bestEffort: Detection is best-effort and depends on consistent formatting being applied throughout the document. Results will be accurate if you used:
docxWarning.styleNames: Final Draft, Fade In, Trelby, or Highland style names, OR
docxWarning.indents: Standard Final Draft indents (Action 1.5", Character 3.5", Dialogue 2.5", Parenthetical 3.0"), OR
docxWarning.patterns: Conventional text patterns (INT./EXT., ALL-CAPS character cues, "CUT TO:" transitions).
docxWarning.unclassified: Anything that can't be classified will be imported as Action and listed in a post-import notice for you to review.
